case_name: Andhra Industrial Works, A. P. v Chief Controller Of Imports And Ors
facts: Andhra Industrial Works, A. P. v Chief Controller Of Imports And Ors
Under Art. 32 of the Constitution of India
issues: The parties and the basic questions for determination are the same.
Whether the respondents have followed the mandatory procedure prescribed in the Import Trade Control Hand Book?
Whether the petitioners' fundamental rights under Arts. 14 and 19 of the Constitution have been violated or imminently threatened.
petitioner_arguments: The petitioners challenge the aforesaid orders of November 7, 1972 passed by Respondent No. 3 on the ground that in view of the Import Policy contained in the Red Book for the relevant period, they were entitled to the grant of these import licences.

The petitioners pray that the impugned orders, dated November 7, 1972, be declared void and a mandamus directing the respondents to issue the licences for the import of the materials in question for the licensing period, April 1969-March 1970, in favour of the petitioners.
respondent_arguments: The respondents have not followed the mandatory procedure prescribed in the Import Trade Control Hand Book.
The respondent could not, in November 1972, grant the licenses applied for to the petitioners in respect of the past period, April 1969-March 1970.
court_reasoning: It must be remembered that the jurisdiction of this Court u/art. 32 can be invoked only for the enforcement of the fundamental rights guaranteed by the Constitution, and not any other legal right.
A petitioner will not be entitled to relief under this Article, unless he establishes that his fundamental right has been violated or imminently threatened.
holding: The respondents are directed to consider and dispose of the applications in accordance with law as expeditiously as possible.
